title: Introduction to Data Mining: Process, Techniques, and Applications

bullets.text: Welcome and overview of data mining's importance in data science.
Defined as extracting useful patterns and trends from large, complex datasets.
Goal is to discover hidden patterns for informed decisions and predictions.
Uncovers relationships impossible or time-consuming to identify manually.
A multi-step process: collect, clean, analyze, model, evaluate, deploy.
Data Collection: Gathering data from diverse sources like logs, sensors, and social media.
Data Preprocessing: Cleaning raw data, handling missing values, duplicates, and standardizing formats.
Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA): Visual and statistical analysis to understand data structure and form hypotheses.
Modeling and Mining: Applying algorithms to uncover patterns and relationships.
Evaluation and Interpretation: Assessing model quality and usefulness of results.
Deployment: Implementing insights into real-world applications for business improvement.
Classification: Assigning data to predefined categories (e.g., email spam detection).
Clustering: Grouping similar data points without prior labels (e.g., customer segmentation).
Association Rule Mining: Identifying relationships between variables (e.g., market basket analysis).
Regression: Predicting continuous values based on inputs (e.g., house price prediction).
Marketing: Tailoring personalized advertisements based on customer segments.
Healthcare: Identifying disease outbreaks and predicting patient readmissions.
Finance: Detecting fraud by analyzing historical transaction patterns.
Retail: Optimizing inventory and forecasting product demand.
Data Quality: Ensuring data is accurate, complete, and unbiased to avoid misleading insights.
Privacy and Ethics: Adhering to regulations like GDPR and CCPA when handling sensitive data.
Requires data anonymization, encryption, and careful handling to mitigate risks.
